collections.name: Pakistani & North Indian
collections.blurb: From S. Abbas Raza, Pakistani & North Indian Cooking (2015), converted to the house recipe standard.
conventions: Heat levels use the book's 1 to 10 dial: high, medium-high (7/10), medium (5/10), medium-low (3/10), low (2/10).
Ginger is measured in cubic inches: 2 cu in is a 1 × 1 × 2 in piece (about 2 × 3 × 5 cm).
Juice of 1 lime is about 2 Tbsp (30 ml).
Green chilies: 3 green chilies = 1 medium jalapeño. Serrano or Thai chilies can replace green chilies one for one, but heat varies widely.
Heat is set at an average Pakistani home level. For milder food, halve the cayenne and green chilies the first time.
Whole spices (cardamoms, cloves, peppercorns) are set aside on the plate, not eaten.
Grind coriander and cumin fresh; make garam masala and garlic/ginger pastes at home (see Basics). Store ground spices airtight.
Oil: any neutral vegetable oil; the book was tested with sunflower oil. Peanut oil for high-heat frying.
Bread: naan or chapati (store-bought frozen is fine); pita or a good baguette in a pinch.
On the side at the table: lime wedges, green chilies, chopped raw onion.
Easiest starting set: Queema Matar, Masoor Daal, Sweet and Sour Green Beans, Plain Basmati Rice.
